# 4 Maccabees Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Conclusion: Epilogue of Praise

---

**1** O children of Israel, descendants of the seed of Abraham, obey this law and live in piety in every way,

**2** knowing that devout reason is the master of all the passions, not only the passions that come from within us but also those that come from outside.

**3** For this reason those men surrendered their bodies to the pain of torments for the sake of God.

**4** And it was through the blood of those devoted ones, and their death as an atoning sacrifice, that divine providence preserved Israel, which had been so severely afflicted.

**5** For the tyrant Antiochus, when he saw the courage of their virtue and their endurance under tortures, proclaimed them to his own soldiers as an example of endurance.

**6** And this produced in his soldiers shame and courage, so that the enemy was unable to subdue the nation by force and gave up the effort.

**7** Thus through the nobility of those who died for God, reason is proved to be sovereign over the passions.

**8** But it would be wrong of me not to recall also the courage of the mother; she deserves even more than praise.

**9** For though she watched seven sons die within the space of a single day, she endured it all heroically because of her hope in God.

**10** She urged each of them on in their ancestral language, filled with noble courage.

**11** She said to them: My sons, I brought you forth from the womb; I nursed you for three years; I raised you and brought you to where you stand today.

**12** I urge you, my children, to look at the sky and the earth and everything in them, and to know that God made them all out of nothing, and that human beings came into existence in the same way.

**13** Do not be afraid of this tormentor. Be worthy of your brothers.

**14** Accept death, so that in God's mercy I may receive you again together with your brothers.

**15** While she was still speaking, the youngest son spoke up and said: O guardians of the law, O friends of virtue, death holds no terror for those who live by virtue.

**16** This most holy and pious mother, filled with joy at the noble deaths of her sons and not overwhelmed by grief at losing them, urged them on to die for God, saying to each of them:

**17** Be courageous, my children! Do not fear death! If you remain faithful to the law, God will grant you a glorious resurrection.

**18** She herself then put the seal on her own faithfulness by following her sons in death.

**19** And I call blessed and holy all those who died in this way for the sake of God.

**20** For they overcame the tyrant through their endurance, and through them their nation was purified.

**21** And so let us conclude: devout reason is the sovereign master of the passions, as the examples of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and their mother have proved beyond any doubt.

**22** They overcame the passions; they conquered the tyrant; they won the prizes of immortality.

**23** They were righteous, and they kept faith with God in life and in death.

**24** Blessed indeed and most holy are the memories of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and the mother, for they fought for the honor of God.

**25** And their souls are now with God, who will honor them forever.
